meta.title: Vigia: a lookout for your Twitch chat
meta.description: Vigia is a free, open-source chat moderator for Twitch streamers: rules in plain language, anti-spoiler protection, OBS highlights and a dashboard for your mods. It runs on your own PC.
hero.eyebrow: Free · Open source · For Twitch streamers
hero.title: A lookout for your chat.
hero.lead: Vigia reads every message in your chat with TypeSafe AI's Jev and does what your rules say: it deletes spam, stops spoilers and puts the best questions on your stream.
hero.note: Pre-release: installers arrive with v1.0. It already runs from source today.

features.title: What a banned-words bot can't do.
f1.title: Rules in plain language
f1.body: Each rule is a yes/no question: "is this unsolicited backseating?". No word lists for chat to learn how to dodge.
f2.title: Real anti-spoiler protection
f2.body: It spots the shape of a spoiler, hides it even from your own dashboard, and loads community packs for the game you're playing.
f3.title: The best of chat, on stream
f3.body: Questions and standout messages go to an OBS overlay, straight away or after a mod approves them.
f4.title: Moderation that doesn't guess
f4.body: It deletes and times out when Jev is sure. When it isn't, the message goes to "Uncertain" and a person decides.
f5.title: A dashboard for you and your mods
f5.body: Live, uncertain, highlights, rules and stats. On your PC, or on your server with Twitch login for your mods.
f6.title: In English and Spanish
f6.body: The interface, the bot and the docs speak both languages. Chat can be in either.
features.commands: And from chat, for you and your mods:
dash.title: Everything happening in your chat, on one screen.
dash.live: Live: every decision with its rule and probability. Possible spoilers stay blurred until you click.
dash.uncertain: Uncertain: whatever Jev wasn't sure about waits for a mod to decide. Vigia never guesses.
dash.alt.live: The Live tab of Vigia's dashboard, with moderated, highlighted and uncertain messages.
dash.alt.uncertain: The Uncertain tab of Vigia's dashboard, with three messages waiting for a decision.
spoilers.title: You never have to write, read or see a spoiler.
spoilers.lead: Three layers that add up, designed so the streamer never finds out anything by accident, not even while setting them up.
s1.title: Jev looks for the shape of a spoiler
s1.body: Deaths, twists, hidden identities, "wait until you see what happens". It knows your game from your Twitch category, and with !vigia progress only what comes later counts.
s2.title: Your mods keep a hidden list
s2.body: They add concrete topics from the dashboard. You only ever see how many there are, never which.
s3.title: Community packs
s3.body: They load by themselves when your category changes. You pick how far you are from part names that spoil nothing.
spoilers.never: Anything flagged as a spoiler is never shown on stream, never quoted by the bot, and blurred in the dashboard.
how.title: Jev answers. Your thresholds decide.
how.1.title: A message arrives
how.1.body: Vigia gathers the text, what it replies to, what its emotes mean and your rules' context. Never the username.
how.2.title: Jev answers with probabilities
how.2.body: All your rules go in one fast call. Jev doesn't write text: it says how likely each "yes" is.
how.3.title: Your thresholds decide
how.3.body: Above "act", the action runs; in the unsure zone, a person decides. You start in observe mode, touching nothing.
how.playground: Drag the thresholds yourself in the playground
install.title: Three ways to run it, all on your own machine.
install.desktop.title: Desktop app
install.desktop.body: Double-click, set it up in one window in about ten minutes, and leave it in the tray while you stream. It updates itself.
install.server.title: Server
install.server.body: For teams: your mods log in with their Twitch account from anywhere.
install.cli.title: Command line
install.cli.body: Try it on any public channel, read-only, with nothing but a Jev key.
install.note: Installers are published with v1.0. Until then, everything works from source.
own.title: Nobody else runs your moderation.
own.1.title: Your keys, your machine
own.1.body: Your own Twitch app and your own Jev key. The author runs no servers, shared apps or proxies.
own.2.title: Private by design
own.2.body: Jev never sees usernames. On desktop, your keys are encrypted with your system's keychain, and history stays on your machine for 7 days.
own.3.title: Costs cents
own.3.body: Jev costs $0.042 per million input tokens, and output is free. The dashboard shows you an hourly estimate.
community.title: Built to grow with the people who use it.
community.body: Spoiler packs for your games, translations, useful rules or code: it's all welcome, and you don't need to code to contribute a pack.
footer.made: Made with TypeSafe AI's Jev. MIT license.
